subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What was the name of the communist guerrilla force fighting in South Vietnam?
questions.explain: The Viet Cong were communist guerrillas who fought US and South Vietnamese forces.

questions.q: Which unpopular, US-backed leader of South Vietnam was overthrown and killed in a 1963 coup?
questions.explain: Ngo Dinh Diem, the US-backed South Vietnamese president, was overthrown and killed in November 1963.

questions.q: At which US university were four students shot dead by the National Guard during anti-war protests in 1970?
questions.explain: Four students were killed at Kent State University in 1970 during protests against the invasion of Cambodia.

questions.q: Following the 1954 Geneva Accords, Vietnam was temporarily divided at which line of latitude?
questions.explain: Vietnam was divided at the 17th parallel into communist North and non-communist South.

questions.q: Which theory held that if one country fell to communism, neighbouring states would follow?
questions.explain: The domino theory drove US fears that the fall of Vietnam would spread communism across Asia.

questions.q: In which year did the Gulf of Tonkin incident lead to a major escalation of US involvement?
questions.explain: The Gulf of Tonkin incident of 1964 led to the resolution authorising fuller US military action.

questions.q: In which year did US forces, under President Nixon, extend the conflict by invading neighbouring Cambodia?
questions.explain: The US invasion of Cambodia in 1970 widened the war and sparked fierce protest at home.

questions.q: What was the chemical defoliant the US sprayed to strip jungle cover from Viet Cong hideouts?
questions.explain: Agent Orange was a herbicide used to destroy jungle cover, causing lasting health and environmental harm.

questions.q: In which year did the Paris Peace Accords lead to the withdrawal of US combat troops from Vietnam?
questions.explain: US combat troops withdrew in 1973 following the Paris Peace Accords.

questions.q: Which US president introduced the policy of 'Vietnamisation' to withdraw American troops gradually?
questions.explain: President Nixon's policy of Vietnamisation handed the fighting over to South Vietnamese forces.

questions.q: Which US president made the major decision to commit large numbers of ground combat troops from 1965?
questions.explain: President Lyndon B. Johnson greatly escalated US ground involvement from 1965 onwards.

questions.q: At which 1954 battle were French forces decisively defeated, ending French rule in Indochina?
questions.explain: The French defeat at Dien Bien Phu in 1954 ended French colonial control of Indochina.

questions.q: What was the name of the supply route running through Laos and Cambodia used to support the Viet Cong?
questions.explain: The Ho Chi Minh Trail carried supplies from North Vietnam to communist forces in the South.

questions.q: In which year did the Viet Cong and North Vietnam launch the Tet Offensive?
questions.explain: The Tet Offensive of 1968 shocked the US public despite being a military setback for the communists.

questions.q: What incendiary weapon, dropped from aircraft, did US forces use against villages and jungle in Vietnam?
questions.explain: Napalm, a burning jelly, was widely used by US forces and caused severe civilian casualties.

questions.q: What was the name of the communist North Vietnamese army that fought alongside the Viet Cong?
questions.explain: The North Vietnamese Army (NVA), or People's Army of Vietnam, fought alongside the southern Viet Cong.

questions.q: What was the name of the 1968 massacre of Vietnamese civilians by US troops?
questions.explain: The My Lai massacre of 1968 saw US soldiers kill hundreds of unarmed civilians, fuelling anti-war feeling.

questions.q: What name was given to the wave of US student and public protest against the war from the late 1960s?
questions.explain: A growing anti-war movement, including student protests, pressured the US government to end the war.

questions.q: Why was the Tet Offensive significant for opinion in the United States?
options: It turned much US public and media opinion against the war
It caused China to enter the war
It proved the US was winning easily
questions.explain: Despite being a military failure for the communists, Tet shifted US media and public opinion against the war.

questions.q: The GCSE topic on the Vietnam conflict broadly covers which span of years?
questions.explain: The Vietnam conflict topic is typically studied across the period 1945 to 1975.

questions.q: In which year did Saigon fall to North Vietnamese forces, ending the war?
questions.explain: The fall of Saigon in April 1975 marked the end of the Vietnam War and the reunification of Vietnam.

questions.q: What tactic, involving hidden tunnels and ambushes, did the Viet Cong rely on against US forces?
questions.explain: The Viet Cong used guerrilla warfare, including the Cu Chi tunnels and surprise ambushes.
